newsitem.title: CHINA: China capital to tighten secrecy rules.
newsitem.headline: China capital to tighten secrecy rules.

text.p: Beijing is considering new regulations to tighten secrecy and stem information leaks in the Chinese capital, city officials and state media said on Thursday.
The new rules, being drafted by city legislators, would strengthen controls on news publishing, scientific research and contacts with foreigners, the China News Service said.
They would also point out that use of the Internet, the worldwide computer network, should not affect state security, it said.
"Organisations that are preparing to report news or release information must first carry out inspections to protect secrecy," the news agency said.
The capital was a vital area for protection of official secrets, it quoted Zhang Yuhong, director of the Beijing State Security Bureau, as saying.
An inspection team in the city had uncovered "200 problems of all sorts" and discovered 130 work units had leaked secrets.
An official of the Beijing government said the capital's lawmakers were expected to approve the new rules soon, but declined to comment further.
China considers a wide range of social, political and economic information to be state secrets and has imposed stiff sentences on journalists and others judged to have broken security regulations.

The new rules stated that neither foreigners involved in "social investigation" nor those who recieved them should touch upon state secrets, the China News Service said without giving further details.
Anyone found leaking secrets must be reported within 24 hours and action should be taken immediately, it said.
